claim_a_counterexample.data: Fix a prime p. S=Spec Z; X1=Y1=Spec F_p; X2=Y2=S; f1=id, f2=id; E1=O_X1 in degree0; E2=the sheaf associated with Z/p in degree0; [a1,b1]=[a2,b2]=[0,0].
claim_a_counterexample.hypotheses: Each required scheme pair is (Spec F_p,Spec Z), whose second factor is S. Tensoring over Z with Z is the identity functor, so all positive Tor groups vanish. The complexes are bounded above. Under f1=id, E1 is a free rank-one module over its own structure sheaf, so its relative Tor amplitude is [0,0]. E2 has only H0.
claim_a_counterexample.external_tensor_identification: X=X1×_S X2=Spec F_p. Under the canonical identification, pr1=id and pr2 corresponds to Z→F_p. Definition1.6 gives Lpr1*(E1)⊗^L_OX Lpr2*(E2). The left term is O_X, and the unit multiplication map identifies this tensor with Lpr2*(E2).
claim_a_counterexample.resolution_and_maps: The complex P=[Z --p→ Z] in degrees−1,0 has an augmentation P→Z/p given in degree0 by quotient and zero elsewhere. Multiplication by p is injective, and its cokernel is Z/p, so this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Both terms are free. Pullback gives F_p⊗_Z P=[F_p --0→ F_p].
claim_a_counterexample.cohomology: H−1=ker(0)=F_p and H0=coker(0)=F_p. Thus the external derived tensor is not acyclic outside the printed summed interval[0,0].
claim_a_counterexample.exact_failure_in_proof: At the relevant points C=B2=A2=Z_(p) and B1=A1=A=B=F_p. The intermediate B⊗^L_B2 M2 is already [F_p --0→ F_p]. Flatness of M1 as a B1-module does not remove this degree−1 cohomology.
claim_a_counterexample.scope: This disproves3.5(a) as printed. It does not disprove3.5(b): for f2=id_S the same E2 has relative Tor amplitude[−1,0], and the product is an object of that summed amplitude. No assertion about all cases of(b) is deduced from this example.

local_ring_identification.exact_map: For x in X1×_S X2 over x1,x2,s, the canonical map O_X1,x1⊗_{O_S,s}O_X2,x2→O_X,x becomes an isomorphism after localization at the inverse image q of the maximal ideal of O_X,x. On affine charts this is the map (R1⊗_R R2) localized first at the elements from R1\p1 and R2\p2 and then at q; these elements are already invertible in (R1⊗_R R2)_p, proving the stated localization identification.
local_ring_identification.counterexample: Take k=Q, S=Spec k, X1=X2=A1_k, and x the generic point of the diagonal u=t. Its two projections are generic points. Set R=k(t)⊗_k k(u), a localization of k[t,u] obtained by inverting all nonzero one-variable polynomials. The ideals q0=(u−t)R and q1=(u−t−1)R are distinct maximal ideals: the evaluation maps u↦t and u↦t+1 have quotient field k(t), and every inverted one-variable polynomial has a nonzero image.
local_ring_identification.failure_and_actual_morphism: The stalk O_X,x is R_q0. The element u−t−1 belongs to q1 and is not a unit of R; it is outside q0 and is a unit of R_q0. Therefore the canonical localization R→R_q0 is not an isomorphism. This proves concretely that the printed unlocalized equality A=A1⊗_C A2 fails.
local_ring_identification.B_equality: Taking Y1=X1,Y2=X2 and f1,f2 identities produces the identical defect for B=B1⊗_C B2.
local_ring_identification.derived_identity: For the same X1,X2 and x, instead take Y1=Y2=S and both f_i the structural maps. All required pairs are Tor-independent because the base is a field. Then B1=B2=B=k, so A1⊗^L_B1 B⊗^L_B2 A2=R in degree0, whereas A=R_q0. The displayed derived identity also lacks the final localization. The explicit comparison is the same localization map R→R_q0.
